definition: A hindrance or obstruction in doing something.
example: The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.

definition: The quality or state of being tranquil; calmness; peacefulness.
example: Seek tranquility of mind: you have power over your judgment of events, not over the events themselves.

definition: Behavior showing high moral standards; a good or useful quality of a thing.
example: Waste no more time arguing about virtue—embody it. Be the good person you describe.

definition: The ability to make considered decisions or come to sensible conclusions.
example: Suspend hasty judgment: everything we hear is an opinion, not a fact; everything we see is a perspective, not the truth.

definition: The development of events beyond a person's control, regarded as determined by a supernatural power.
example: Accept the things to which fate binds you, and love the people with whom fate brings you together, but do so with all your heart.

definition: The capacity to recover quickly from difficulties; toughness.
example: Resilience is choosing not to be harmed—and so not feeling harmed; refuse the injury, and you have not been injured.

definition: A view or judgment formed about something, not necessarily based on fact or knowledge.
example: Everything we hear is an opinion, not a fact. Everything we see is a perspective, not the truth.

definition: A particular attitude toward or way of regarding something; a point of view.
example: Everything we see is a perspective, not the truth.

definition: The action of consenting to receive or undertake something offered; agreement to an offer or proposal.
example: Practice acceptance of the things to which fate binds you, and love the people with whom fate brings you together.

definition: The state of being subject to death; the quality or state of being mortal.
example: Fear not mortality itself, but never beginning to live while you still draw breath.

definition: The action of inflicting hurt or harm on someone for an injury or wrong suffered at their hands.
example: The best revenge is to be unlike him who performed the injury.

definition: Importance requiring swift action.
example: Act with urgency: do not live as if you had ten thousand years; death hangs over you—while it is in your power, be good.

definition: In Stoic thought, the rational principle ordering the cosmos and human reason.
example: Live according to logos: let reason, not impulse, write the next line of your day.

definition: Training that develops self-control, character, or efficiency.
example: Discipline of perception is the first freedom—see clearly before you act.

definition: The state of not lasting forever; transience.
example: Impermanence is not a threat to meaning; it is the reason this hour matters.

definition: Mental calmness and composure, especially in difficulty.
example: Equanimity is not numbness—it is strength that refuses to be jerked by every rumor.

definition: At home in the whole world; a citizen of everywhere
example: Aurelius calls himself cosmopolitan: his city is Rome, but as a man, the world.

definition: The state of being equal, especially in rights
example: Meditations admires a polity built on parity: equal rights and equal freedom of speech for all.

definition: A settled calm; freedom from being thrown about by events.
example: Ataraxia is not numbness; it is a mind that has stopped arguing with what it cannot command.
speech: You Have Power Over Your Mind

definition: In Stoic teaching, freedom from passions that overthrow reason.
example: Apatheia does not mean you feel nothing. It means feeling is no longer your master.
speech: You Have Power Over Your Mind

definition: The Stoic faculty of moral choice, the will that judges what appears.
example: Prohairesis — the choice that is yours — is the only kingdom he tells you to govern.
speech: You Have Power Over Your Mind

definition: The mind's agreement to an impression, which makes it yours.
example: Do not give assent to the first story your anger tells you.
speech: You Have Power Over Your Mind

definition: A division into two opposed kinds; here, what is up to you and what is not.
example: The dichotomy is simple and severe: some things are up to you, and the rest are not.
speech: You Have Power Over Your Mind

definition: Things outside one's moral control, such as reputation, health, and the acts of others.
example: Externals can be taken. Your response to them cannot, unless you hand it over.
speech: You Have Power Over Your Mind

definition: The way the mind takes an event, which is where freedom begins.
example: Change the perception, he writes, and you have changed the only thing you can actually change.
speech: You Have Power Over Your Mind

definition: Inner unease that signals a judgment still unexamined.
example: Disquiet is a signal to examine a judgment, not an order to obey it.
speech: You Have Power Over Your Mind

definition: An appearance presented to the mind before one has judged it.
example: An impression is not yet a fact. Wait, and see what it is before you suffer it.
speech: You Have Power Over Your Mind

definition: A rational or divine order within which one still must do one's duty.
example: To accept providence is not to call every loss good. It is to do your part inside what arrives.
speech: You Have Power Over Your Mind
